clue.text: Drug addict should stop behaving like that!

definitions.text: Drug addict should stop behaving like that!

parts.words: Drug addict should stop behaving like that!
parts.note: the exclamation telling someone to stop pretending is read literally as advice to an addict to get off the drug

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an everyday retort meaning 'stop pretending'; here it is also what an addict should literally do, quit the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a scornful order to drop a pretence, exactly what 'stop behaving like that' says.

clue.text: Inferior guy securing Egyptian flag

indicators.note: a guy securing a letter holds it fast inside himself, so the letter goes within the word

parts.note: a guy is a chap
E is the abbreviation for Egyptian
a jack is a small flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.surface: A second-rate fellow is clutching an Egyptian banner.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word describes shoddy, cheap goods, so it fits 'inferior'.

clue.text: Doctor to treat black eye

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
to treat something can be to use it, as in treating one's tools well

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to see to a patient's bruised eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruised, darkened eye is called this in slang, from its swelling like a small rodent.

clue.text: Unexceptional old American bicycle

definitions.meaning: the high-wheeled penny-farthing type of cycle was called this in America and Britain

explanation.surface: An unremarkable vintage bike from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Commonplace things are run-of-the-mill; the high-wheel cycle took the name to distinguish it from the later safety bicycle.

clue.text: Previous state adopted by iron

indicators.note: a state taken in by iron sits inside the chemical symbol, as a child is taken into a family

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Oregon is a US state

explanation.surface: A former political status taken on by a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone before is past or prior, as in a foregone age.

clue.text: Bar of soap, say, permitted to be added to bill

indicators.note: the second word joins on after the first, so it is appended to the bill

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A soap bar is allowed on the hotel bill as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake of soap is a tablet, a flat compressed block; 'say' marks it as one example.

clue.text: American tool used by 7 is saw

parts.note: the American spelling of axe is ax
the answer to 7 down, the island in the Irish Sea, is abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: An American cutting tool used on an island is a saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like another tool alongside the axe, but here it means a wise saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, a self-evident truth.

clue.text: A pound added to some capital in the States

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Another pound is added to some money in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in the surface; it is a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the state capital of New York, a capital city in the United States.

clue.text: Venue for races in a film one's shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film about someone being shot is set at the racing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'one's' counts as a letter here. The island hosts the TT motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: The island in the Irish Sea is famous for its TT motorcycle road races.

clue.text: Note car on motorway

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A memo about a car on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note, a half note lasting two crotchets.

clue.text: Country allocating money to road construction

parts.note: the ecu was the European currency unit, and an old French coin

indicators.note: construction means building something new, here a new order for the word road

explanation.surface: A nation earmarks money for road building.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American country.

clue.text: Overprotect half our capital in the City

parts.note: to baby someone is to pamper or overprotect them

indicators.note: half of the six-letter capital is taken, the second three letters being dropped

parts.note: for a London newspaper, our capital is London

explanation.surface: A Londoner is too protective of half the City's workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' drops DON from LONDON, leaving LON. 'the City' suggests London's financial district, but the city is the ancient one.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the great ancient city on the Euphrates.

clue.text: Farm labourer goes about a foot

indicators.note: the labourer goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a peon is a farm labourer in Latin America

explanation.surface: A field hand walks about on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is a metrical foot in verse, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody it is a metrical unit of one long and three short syllables.

clue.text: Author said play could provide what resting actors need

indicators.note: said means the author's name is heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
play means room for movement, as in a rope with some play

explanation.surface: A writer claims a play could give actors their rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a drama; it means room, scope.
explanation.definitionFit: The lounge backstage where performers wait and relax offstage is so called.

clue.text: Dad's backing Mum, perhaps — that's evident

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for dad is turned round

parts.note: pa is dad
a mum is one example of a mother or father

explanation.surface: Father supports mother; it is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain to see, obvious, clearly visible.

clue.text: Hobby of some recently seen in pursuit of letter

indicators.note: something in pursuit of another follows behind it, so this word comes second

parts.note: phi is a Greek letter
lately means recently

explanation.surface: Recently some people have taken up chasing letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' in the surface hints at mail, and stamp collecting is indeed about letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collecting is a pastime pursued by some enthusiasts.

clue.text: Runner reaching half-way point is complacent

indicators.note: a runner who has reached half-way stops there, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a runner is a smuggler of contraband, as in gun-runner

explanation.surface: An athlete reaching the half-way mark is self-satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is a smuggler, of which the first half is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-satisfied and pleased with oneself.

clue.text: Bloomer gondolier might make if daughter takes one's place

indicators.note: a gondolier might make something of his letters, rearranging them
one is the letter I, and the daughter's letter replaces it

explanation.surface: A Venetian boatman might make a blunder if his daughter took over.
explanation.walkthrough: With D in place of I the letters GONDOLDER are rearranged. 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a yellow-flowered plant, something that blooms.

clue.text: Staircase containing an opening for ventilation

indicators.note: the staircase holds the other word within it

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: A stairwell has a vent for air.
explanation.definitionFit: The small window above a door can be opened to let in air and light.

clue.text: Worker sometimes unpunctual, forming a pattern

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
late means behind time, as a worker sometimes is

explanation.surface: A worker who is often late sets a bad example.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide or model shape used to produce copies.

clue.text: King's knight moved back — it could be used in incisive attack

definitions.text: it could be used in incisive attack

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: moved back means turned backwards, like a chess piece retreating

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A chess king's knight retreats, ready for a cutting attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: 'incisive' means cutting, and the weapon is a Malay dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade, used for stabbing.

clue.text: Parental, in a way

indicators.note: in a way can mean in another arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Being a parent, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fatherly is one way of being a parent.

clue.text: Something like an inch taken from slip in blue

indicators.note: in places the slip inside the word for blue

parts.note: sky is used for a sky-blue colour
to err is to make a slip

explanation.surface: A small measure is taken away from a slip in the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'inch' is Scottish for a small island, not the measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a rocky islet, much like a Scottish inch, a small island.

clue.text: Gang joined by Italian robber

parts.note: a band is a gang
It is an abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A gang joined by an Italian thief.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw who steals, often by force.

clue.text: Vote against accepting seven points for this

definitions.meaning: to reject a candidate for membership by secret vote
in snooker potting the highest-valued ball scores seven points

explanation.surface: Voting no while taking seven points.
explanation.definitionFit: A club rejection was once cast with a dark ball; in snooker the dark ball is worth seven.

clue.text: He'S gone to pot, according to Keats

definitions.text: He'S gone to pot, according to Keats

parts.words: He'S gone to pot, according to Keats
parts.note: in Keats's poem Isabella buries her murdered lover's head in a garden pot in which a herb grows

explanation.walkthrough: 'gone to pot' normally means deteriorated; here the herb is literally in a pot, from Keats's 'Isabella, or the Pot of Basil'.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb grew in the pot holding Lorenzo's head in Keats's poem.

clue.text: Put out by climax in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: a peak is a climax, the highest point

explanation.surface: Annoyed at the high point of a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' is an adjective, irritated, matching the noun-as-verb sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is to feel resentment, irritated or offended.

clue.text: One engineer understanding question paper — a lot

indicators.note: read as under-standing: in a down answer the following letters stand below the question

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: An engineer who grasps the question paper well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understanding' looks like comprehension but means standing under.
explanation.definitionFit: A quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of writing material.

clue.text: He's read version that's cut

indicators.note: a version is a different form of something, so the letters appear in a new order

explanation.surface: He has read a translation that has been abridged.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped, trimmed, as sheep's wool is shorn.

clue.text: Finally firing more work-shy workman

indicators.note: finally picks the very last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: lazier means more work-shy

explanation.surface: A lazier workman is finally sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits panes into windows.

clue.text: Reserve parking place

definitions.meaning: a roadside pull-in where cars can stop

explanation.surface: A reserved parking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To put by for later is to save; a roadside stopping area off the carriageway also bears the name.

clue.text: It proves ownership of river in noble setting

indicators.note: in places the river inside the other word
the noble word is a setting, a mount holding a stone, for the river

parts.note: titled means having a noble title
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Proof of owning a river set in noble estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal document showing who owns a property.
